title: 0582-developing-a-ranking-problem-library-rplib
universal_lens: {'structural_mathematical_unification': 'RPLIB introduces β, a novel rankability measure that quantifies the location of ambiguity in optimal ranking sets, extending the classical trio (k, |P|, τ) to capture where indecisiveness occurs in a ranking.'}
gsi_mapping: {'bayesian_conformal_mapping': "In GSI's Bayesian posterior inference over NFL team states, β serves as a conformal diagnostic: when β is low, the posterior distribution is sharply peaked (low uncertainty), whereas high β indicates multimodality or spread across the ranking, signaling that more data or stronger priors are needed to resolve ambiguity."}
gse_mapping: {'situational_reasoning_mapping': "For GSE's state-transition models, β flags situations where the current state (team performance matrix) yields multiple optimal rankings. High β at the top of the ranking triggers a switch to conservative actions (e.g., hedging bets on multiple outcomes) rather than committing to a single predicted order."}

primitives.verbatim_quote: - β (Figure 12, definition shown graphically in the paper): a weighted function of the number and location of fractional entries of the X̄* matrix from the linear ordering model — penalises fractional entries that are further from the diagonal and lower in the ranking.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'beta': 'Dimensionless', 'x_bar_star': 'Binary matrix (n x n), where n is the number of items being ranked'}
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exponential growth in computational complexity as the size of the optimal face increases; practical limits occur when the number of optimal rankings exceeds feasible storage or enumeration thresholds.

layer2.mapping: β maps directly to the concept of 'information entropy' in statistical mechanics, measuring disorder in the optimal solution set. In GSE, it corresponds to 'state ambiguity'—the degree to which multiple future trajectories are equally likely given current telemetry.
layer2.telemetry: Observed via Monte-Carlo sampling of the posterior distribution over rankings; higher variance in sampled centroids indicates higher β.
